---
title: "Roxygen suggestions"
description: "Claude reviews and rewrites roxygen2 documentation."
---

`roxygen-suggest.yml` has Claude review the roxygen2 block of each function
whose file changed since the last review (see
[what gets reviewed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-reviewed)), or of every
function in a [full review](suggestions.qmd#full-review), for
completeness and accuracy against its code. It proposes an improved block
as a [suggestion PR](suggestions.qmd).

## What it changes

- **Only six parts are rewritten**: title, description, details,
  parameters, return value and examples. Every other tag — `@export`,
  `@importFrom`, `@seealso`, `@rdname`, … — is kept exactly as written.
- **Exported and internal functions** get different guidance, e.g. examples
  are required only for exported ones.
- **Style**: explicit `@title` / `@description` tags, tags in a fixed
  order, examples wrapped in `\dontrun{}`. Order and guidance are set in
  `config/roxygen-style.yml` and can be
  [adjusted](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance).
- **One function per file** is assumed: only the first function of a file
  is reviewed.
- **Only real improvements**: Claude gives a reason for every change.
  Changes that only make correct text clearer or restyle it are dropped,
  as are changes in whitespace, punctuation or case only — those parts
  keep your original lines. See
  [what gets proposed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed). This also
  holds for a title or description written without a tag (the first
  lines of the block): unless it is changed, it stays as it is.

If a block is already adequate, nothing is proposed.

## The report

The link comment on your PR and the suggestion PR's description start with
a one-line summary, e.g. "8 changes applied · 3 not applied · 1 possible
bug". The description is
[one report](suggestions.qmd#one-suggestion-pr-per-branch), rebuilt on
every run, with collapsible sections:

- **Applied changes**, grouped per file, each with its reason, a short
  explanation and a [checkbox](suggestion-choices.qmd) to decline it;
- **Not applied**, grouped per reason (e.g. `clarity`), with Claude's
  proposed text — tick one to apply it;
- **Possible bugs in the code** that Claude noticed while checking the
  documentation against the code. Nothing in the code is changed.

Each finding names the commit it came from. With a suggestion PR open, a
later run reviews the documentation **the PR proposes** (unless you
edited it since), so the same fixes aren't suggested again; Claude also
judges the earlier findings, and those that no longer hold are crossed
out with the reason.

**Possible bugs** are judged before they are reported: Claude first
explains its reasoning, then gives a verdict and how sure it is. Only
verdicts of a real defect are kept, at high or medium confidence by
default — set with the input `code-issue-confidence` (`none`: not
looked for). Without a suggestion PR, they are posted as a comment on
your PR, or, without a PR, collected in one issue per month ("Roxygen
sweep: possible bugs in the code (YYYY-MM)"). That's why the caller
grants `issues: write`; see [where reports go](suggestions.qmd#where-reports-go).

Heading sizes and spacing can be adjusted in `config/report-style.yml`
([per repository](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance)); GitHub
doesn't allow custom fonts or spacing, so the options are heading levels
and blank lines.

## DataSHIELD packages

With `datashield-type` set, Claude gets role-specific guidance
(the default `none` is for other packages):

| `datashield-type` | For | Guidance |
|---|---|---|
| `client` | client packages | functions that send calls to the servers, e.g. what is returned locally vs. computed server-side |
| `server` | server packages | functions that compute on the servers' data |
| `utility` | analyst-side helper packages, e.g. for setting up analysis projects or mock data | side effects on the analyst's machine; examples that write only to `tempdir()` |

- **Login example:** client packages listed in
  `config/datashield-example-env.yml` get a ready-made multi-study login
  to the Opal demo server for their examples. Utility packages get it
  through the client packages they depend on (e.g. `dsBaseClient`), and
  only for functions that work on DataSHIELD connections (a `datasources`
  argument, or `datashield.*()` / `ds.*()` calls).
- **Typos stop the run:** any other `datashield-type` stops it with an
  error, so a typo can't silently drop the guidance.
